Hi Luka — for this build, please populate J\_DISP\_LED this way:

\- Use BSS138 as the low-side switch; GPIO42 PWM controls brightness.
\- Fit a 20kΩ gate resistor plus a 20kΩ gate pull-down; the latter keeps the LED off during boot.
\- Populate the 5V jumper on Pin 1, and leave the 3V3 jumper footprint empty.
\- Connect a 9.4µF X5R 0603 capacitor from Pin 1 to GND for PWM ripple decoupling.
\- Leave the series-resistor footprint DNP because the LED strip self-limits.
\- Do not add a flyback diode, since the LED load is resistive rather than inductive.

For context, the e-paper has no built-in light, so an external LED behind it will provide the backlight. The final LED has not been chosen yet: I am testing a 5V COB strip first and may later switch to a 3.3V frontlight module, so both must be supported by the circuit.

At ~140mA in the worst case (10W/m strip × 134mm cut), the load remains well within the 400mA rating of the BSS138.

Only as a fallback for a future bare-LED option, retain the 3V3 jumper and DNP series R footprint; leaving both empty now costs nothing.

Under the J\_DISP\_LED rows / pinout / Critical Routing, the full specification is available in <http://board-package-v2.example|pcb-integrated-v2.md>.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
I found a few items that may or may not be problems. Please tell me which are genuine issues; if any are not, that is fine, but explain why:

1\. For buttons 3 and 4 and the slide switch, CN17 / CN19 / CN20 connect the GPIO nets to GND when pressed. However, R16 / R17 / R18 are also pull-downs to GND on those same nets, so the GPIO would read LOW when pressed and LOW when released. Should those resistors instead be pull-UPS to +3V3, or should connector pin 1 receive +3V3?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Pin 28, VRTC, on the AXP2101 is currently unconnected, although the datasheet calls for a 100 nF capacitor between VRTC and GND. Was that deliberate, or was it overlooked?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: The ESP32 module’s C18 (0.2 µF) and C19 (47 µF) decoupling capacitors sit 12–15 mm from its 3V3 pin (pin 2), while the specification calls for no more than 4 mm. Could we place a small 0.2 µF capacitor closer to that pin? The bulk C19 can remain where it is.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Although the AXP2101 / MT3608 decoupling works, it is less compact than the typical reference: the AXP2101 capacitors are 3.0–8.0 mm from the QFN edge, while the MT3608 C4/C5 output capacitors are 6–9 mm from the package edge. candidates.speaker: client

Are you comfortable with the possible slight reduction in WiFi range from leaving those parts in the secondary keepout, or should we try to clear it?

candidates.speaker: client

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Could you bring the currently unconnected AXP2101 PWROK (pin 29) and VBACKUP (pin 27) out to small test pads or vias beside the AXP2101? Exposing VBACKUP would let us later fit a backup capacitor or coin cell for RTC retention or wake-from-off, while PWROK would be available for debugging. These should be signal traces only, not power, so the change should be quick.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: I’ll check the documentation now; in the meantime, leave the capacitors unchanged.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thanks, Luka. Everything is clear:
1. For v4, leave VRTC NC because this board has no external RTC chip. On the RTC topic, I realized that I previously mixed up VRTC with VBACKUP. VBACKUP (pin 27) supplies backup power to keep the AXP2101's internal RTC running after the main battery is removed. Could you expose VBACKUP on a small test pad or via beside PWROK from item #10? This would let us later install a 200 µF capacitor for \~8-10 min of hot-swap tolerance, a supercap for several weeks, or a CR1220 coin cell for \~9 years of real time-keeping. Nothing needs to be populated now; only expose the pad.
2. For the buttons (R16/R17/R18), agreed: convert all three to pull-ups at 3V3. They remain active LOW, with connector pin 1 tied to GND and a press shorting the GPIO input to GND. I updated <http://board-package.example|pcb-integrated.md> to reflect this.
3. The PIR (R19) and Touch (R20/R25) circuits are already correct as pull-downs and need no changes. Both the AM312 (PIR) and TTP223 (touch) provide push-pull active-HIGH outputs, so their internal drivers override the 20 k pull-down while active. The pull-down to GND simply ensures a defined LOW state whenever a sensor is unplugged.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: For VBUS and BAT−, which see the worst-case simultaneous current of up to ~3.2 A from 2.4 A charging plus ~0.8 A system load, I need confirmation on two points. First, do the F.Cu and In2.Cu pours remain contiguous from the USB-C or battery connector through to the AXP2101 VBUS and BAT pins, without any thin trace in series? Second, are there enough stitching vias between F.Cu and In2.Cu on those nets—typically 6+ vias for ~3.2 A? If both conditions are met, I am happy with the design. What concerns me is any 0.4 mm series bottleneck, since a 0.4 mm outer-layer trace carrying 3 A would run hot, with about a ~60 °C rise over ambient.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: In that case, the design is acceptable and no further changes are needed for this issue.

The factory’s latest detail may support the theory: VBUS and VSYS are normal on all 3 boards, and both sets of pins lie along the top edge of the AXP2101. On the right edge are the DCDC1 pins—FB1, LX1, and VIN1—and that is precisely the side failing on the 2 bad boards.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: To restore ESD protection properly, please correct the symbol: connect pin 5 (VBUS) to +5V, route pin 2 separately to GND instead of tying the two together, and retain the D+/D- pass-through via U3. When USBLC6 is wired correctly, protection returns and USB operates. Is that what you intend to change? There is no rush; I will continue testing meanwhile.
